name: Simulated stakeholder polling: synthetic electorates and twin panels
one_line: Trace- or interview-grounded synthetic respondents, poststratified, nowcast approval / sentiment prints and under-polled races for Polymarket's poll-print brackets and thin election markets; unproven, and a no-AI random walk on the published number already ties the weekly approval price.
maturity: Experimental; one prospective scored synthetic poll (PoSSUM, 50/51 states, 2.6-pt bias, 61% of results inside 90% intervals), retrospective Korean 3/3 after Gallup recalibration, vendor claims only otherwise; nobody trades it; literature says item means, not change
requires_ai: yes; LLM respondents answer the exact poll question; MrP, debiasing and sizing statistical
edge: Hypothetical: opinion-drift signal between real polls, or a poll where none exists
capital: <$1k-$5k; capacity-bound ($6-93 within 5c per bracket), data costs dominate
build_time: 3-6 weeks solo on file 21's stack; +2-4 weeks per country for MrP frames
opportunity_size: Weekly approval brackets $21-69k/month Jun-Sep 2026 (down ~90% from 2025's ~$530k/month); 96 thin non-US races trading >= $100/day
expected_results: no public data, theoretical only; guess -$75 to +$75/month before LLM and data costs; no-AI rule is a file-20 hypothesis
competition: no synthetic-poll trader found; hobbyists, stat modellers, reward quoters set prices
flag: grey; GDPR Art. 9, consent, never publish synthetic polls, election-contract restrictions
validate: Post-cutoff replay on weekly approval brackets vs real-time carry-forward and market; kill if debiased delta = carry-forward
top_risk: No-AI carry-forward already ties the market; panels miss change
solo_fit_reason: Cheap to kill-test on weekly brackets, but silicon respondents recover item means and country priors, not individual or week-to-week change (3.05% of respondent variance; neighbour-country average beats every LLM condition); a random walk on the chart version published before each forecast already ties the market (Brier 0.122 / 0.121 / 0.103 vs 0.122 / 0.126 / 0.100 at 5 / 3 / 1 days); near-mid depth is $1-93 per bracket and proving a 0.01 per-bracket gain needs ~48-129 weekly events.
speed_class: speed-insensitive: daily panel runs; the edge is weekly drift; poll-release race is file 17
results_5k: marginal; -$760 to -$180/month with one synthetic poll a month (guess)
results_10k: not as sized; -$1,950 to -$580/month, capacity and data costs (guess)
min_capital: $0 until the kill test passes; ~$1k in weekly brackets after
capacity_ceiling: ~$2-5k: ~$1.5k/month near-mid bracket turnover plus a few thin races
services: Silver Bulletin approval series (Datawrapper CSV, vintages)
monthly_running_cost: minimum ~$30-60; comfortable ~$700-1,500; plus $1.5-3.2k per real micro-poll
changes_made: Written 2026-09-29 with live checks: Gamma approval / umich / elections events (174 closed approval events, 80 weekly bracket events with 481 markets, 1,754 open election events), Silver Bulletin approval series from the page's public Datawrapper CSV (616 daily values, six older vintages compared), CLOB prices-history on all 481 bracket markets at three horizons, CLOB books on the live October 2 event, Kalshi poll-print series and KXAPRPOTUS volumes, arXiv API abstracts for 12 papers, PoSSUM HTML, Fortune on Aaru, Simile site, HF API for Twin-2K-500, GitHub / HN searches, X API pricing, GDPR Art. 9, PBS and Ruffini on the August 2026 fake polls, Polymarket fee docs.

Own baseline: the Silver Bulletin value on each resolution date falls in the resolved bracket in 80 of 80 events; history is never revised except the provisional latest day (up to 0.68 pt); the series is a random walk (daily SD 0.24, lag-1 autocorrelation 0.01).

Own baseline: market Brier per bracket 0.122 / 0.126 / 0.100 at 5 / 3 / 1 days vs 0.123 / 0.125 / 0.113 for a leave-future-out random walk on the last finalised value (event-clustered CIs include zero at 5 and 3 days; market better at 1 day); with one-day-fresher data the random walk ties at all horizons; 50/50 blend CIs include zero.
No-AI rule (|random walk - mid| > 10c, 2c half-spread, fee) +7.9c/share at 3 days [+0.7, +15.4] on 135 trades; only one of six cells excludes zero; recorded as a hypothesis for file 20.

Brief's capacity figures updated: weekly bracket family now $21-69k/month (from $0.2-1.1M in 2025); UMich four events ($184k, $24k, $42k, $13k), none open; live bracket depth $6-93 within 5c, rewards $72/day across the event.
Brief's fake-poll headline resolved to PBS (Median Strategies: Kalshi Bass 63c -> 65c in 15 min; ~20 Polymarket accounts traded within 6 min) and Ruffini (paywalled intro).

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-29 (26 numbered sources re-fetched or re-queried: 12 arXiv abstracts via the API, PoSSUM and Dynamo-K full text, Fortune, Simile, PBS/AP, Ruffini, X API pricing, GDPR Art. 9, Polymarket fee docs, HF and GitHub APIs, HN Algolia, Kalshi API, Gamma and CLOB; 26 confirmed or corrected, 0 removed, 0 unreachable; E8 / E9 claims checked against the packs): (1) the writer's own open doubt resolved: Datawrapper version Last-Modified headers (1,364 versions, monotone) show the previous day's provisional point is always on the chart at 00:00 UTC, so the writer's random-walk arm was one day staler than necessary; rebuilding the arm from the 238 versions actually published before each forecast time (no look-ahead) gives Brier 0.122 / 0.121 / 0.103 vs market 0.122 / 0.126 / 0.100, every interval straddling zero: the market's apparent one-day win was an artefact; power SDs and event counts recomputed (48 / 79 / 129 events for 0.01 per bracket). (2) The no-AI threshold rule re-priced with the real-time arm at 2-4c half-spreads and today's fee: +9.9c at 3c (+2.1 to +17.8c), +8.9c at 4c, other cells nothing, Bonferroni over nine cells includes zero, 331 of 481 brackets fee-free when traded; kept as a file-20 hypothesis worth tens of dollars a month. (3) Resolution: 4 of 80 events had a disputed first UMA proposal (three No proposals on brackets that resolved Yes) while /v2/resolutions reports was_disputed false on all four. Also: Dynamo-K's 3/3 is 'best case' with a 29-100% CI and uses Gallup recalibration (97% of moderate agents vote progressive unmitigated; MAE 36.8 -> 7.1); PoSSUM's 61% is coverage of 90% intervals and the refusals came from GPT-4o's instruction hierarchy; Aaru's Harris +4.2 is a September projection; PBS piece is AP; volume history corrected ($0.22-1.12M Mar 2025-Feb 2026, $373k Apr, $158k May, $21-69k Jun-Sep; down ~90%); second book snapshot (2-4c spreads, $1-88 within 5c, rewards $50/day); added value-of-information arithmetic for the hybrid micro-poll tier (brief scope item). 15-field part 2,516 -> 2,485 words after additions.
open_doubts: The real-time arm assumes the forecast is made at 00:00 UTC with the chart as published then; intraday timing against Silver Bulletin's ~14-17 daily publishes was not modelled.
Market prices are hourly prices-history points, not executable quotes; the rule's PnL assumes a fixed 2-4c half-spread while live books move between 2c and 8c spreads and hold $1-93 within 5c.
The power figures use the carry-forward-vs-market difference as a proxy; a synthetic delta arm's variance is unknown.
Twin-panel and PoSSUM-style cost figures are design estimates (tokens, X API reads), not measured runs.
The non-US election classification is by title and tag keywords; counts (275 / 238 / 96) are approximate.
Kalshi volumes are contracts, not dollars; Gamma volumes count both legs of each fill; three March 2026 approval events report zero Gamma volume.
Whether reusing Silver Bulletin's chart data for a trading model is permitted by its terms was not checked.
